# Brain contract and decisions

Doctrine 0.1.0. What each acting answer does, and the observer -> planner -> guarded controller -> executor -> audit contract the brain must honour.

## Brain decisions (what each acting answer does, and when to give it)

- **ACT-01** (p1) An acting answer only brings forward what the engine would do later, or picks one of the engine's own modes: start the ramp (P0 to P1), end the ramp (P1 to P2), end the day's watering (P2 to P3), steer, hold or decay the EC offset, set a probe aside, or one notch on the zone's maintenance shot size or re-water threshold. Code acts only on a firm answer, so a split answer moves nothing, and the envelope refuses anything outside its bounds. When nothing acts, the engine decides exactly as it would without a brain. — `product-rule` · BRAIN, ENGINE, PSO
- **ACT-02** (p1) Starting the ramp (dawn): start when the plants are drinking (moisture falling steadily since lights-on, much as on previous mornings) and the slab has dried a little since lights-on; keep drying while the trace is flat after lights-on (the plants are not transpiring yet); answer probe_not_moving when the reading has not changed for a long time. The evidence measures the morning drop against dryback_target, which on many installs is set far above any morning drop: being far from it is not by itself a reason to wait. Code admits a start only part-way into P0 (BR-2). — `product-rule` · BRAIN, ENGINE, CTRL, VND-IRRIGATION, OSS-CTRL
- **ACT-03** (p1) Ending the ramp (ramp): hand over (slab_full, ec_is_feed_front or real_salt) when the last shots no longer lift the retained moisture, or spike and fall straight back, with moisture at or near the ceiling. High pore EC in the first 45 minutes after a shot, with feed below it, is the feed front passing; genuinely high salt also hands over, because maintenance runoff is what removes it. Keep ramping while shots still lift moisture that stays; answer probe_lagging when the last shot has not shown yet. The engine's own rise rule also ends P1, but when the curve already shows full, handing over is right, not redundant. Code admits it only near the ceiling with the minimum ramp shots in (BR-2). — `product-rule` · BRAIN, ENGINE, GL-PROBE, GL-LAW
- **ACT-04** (p1) Ending the day's watering (dusk) is the brain's overnight-dryback lever. Enter P3 now when the zone is steered generative, is well above its re-water threshold and the rescue floor, and its observed overnight dryback has been running under the stage's band (when the evidence gives one). Give one more top-up first when the zone is close to its threshold or pore EC is well above target with a dilutive feed (that answer itself moves nothing). Continue P2 when the overnight dryback has been running deep, the zone is low, or it is too early. The 'overnight dryback target' in the evidence is dryback_target measured from the day's peak, often far deeper than any arc band: weigh the converted arc band, not that figure. Code admits P3 only in the last 3 hours, only for a zone steered generative and never near the rescue floor (BR-2). After it the overnight rescue shot still fires, and while the lights stay on so do the watchdog and any configured floor, except on a tick a maximum-EC block or hold stops every shot (IR-2, IR-3). — `product-rule` · BRAIN, ENGINE, VND-IRRIGATION, GL-SLAB
- **ACT-05** (p1) The EC steer's mode (salt), asked in P2 while EC stacking is on: name what drives pore EC and code picks the mode. Salt building against a weaker feed, or EC rising after flush water (the salt front still passing): steer. The feed changing, EC inside its band, or below its band in a vegetative stage: hold. EC readings that jump or disagree with the moisture, or a target nothing on this feed has reached: decay (the offset halves every 30 minutes toward none). Keep the same answer while the evidence is unchanged; a new mode needs new evidence, not a new half hour. Without a measured feed EC the weaker-feed test is unverified (FEED-01), so do not call salt building on it alone. — `product-rule` · BRAIN, CTRL, ENGINE, GL-ROCKWOOL
- **ACT-06** (p1) Setting a probe aside (probe): answer from the shots. Water went in: did the reading rise, did most of the rise stay, and did it dry back between shots, as the zone's own history and its siblings show? A reading that stays high and flat while shots fire, rises for other zones' shots, or spikes and falls straight back is not tracking: give a low probability of yes and name the failure mode. Calling it sound when the shots say otherwise keeps the engine watering on a bad reading, and on a default install, past the morning ramp, nothing else waters a zone whose probe sits high (PRB-08). Code sets the probe aside only after two agreeing answers in a row and its own confirmation (BR-3); the zone then copies a healthy sibling or waters on a timer within its budget, and a later answer that the probe tracks restores it. — `product-rule` · BRAIN, CTRL, GL-PROBE
- **ACT-07** (p1) Tomorrow's maintenance notch (setpoints): pick one of smaller shots, bigger shots, later re-water, sooner re-water, or keep. Bigger shots drain more and bring pore EC down; smaller shots drain less and let it climb; a later re-water dries the zone further between shots and sends it into the night drier (a larger overnight dryback); a sooner re-water does the opposite. Code moves the zone's own number one 0.5 notch, at most once a grow-day, inside a band around the last value of that number the brain did not write (BR-5). That centre is not always the grower's: this question is asked only with Auto Setpoints on, the learner shifts the threshold with field capacity (CT-12), and any value the brain did not write becomes the band's new centre, so the band moves with the learner and the evidence's 'your value' may be the learner's. A notch is a step from wherever the zone now stands. A rescue shot soon after a change puts the value from before it back and pauses the zone's notches (BR-6). Keep when the zone is on course, and do not answer a learner move or an over_saturated label (CT-14) with a notch. — `product-rule` · BRAIN, CTRL, ENGINE, VND-IRRIGATION
- **ACT-08** (p1) Every other question advises: whether a shot landed, whether an overnight fall is drying or the probe, why a zone's water differs from its siblings', how the zone sits against its stage arc, and the room report and why answers. They never move water. Name what the evidence shows; a setting the brain cannot move (dryback target, P0 wait, EC targets, P1 target, field capacity, rescue floor, maximum EC, daily budget and floor, EC stacking, the feed) is a recommendation for a person, worded as one. With Auto Setpoints on, code moves field capacity and the P1 target toward the zone's own peaks, at most a point a grow-day, and never moves the rescue floor (CT-12): a value typed into those two is moved from, not kept, so the recommendation names the cause (probe, delivery, ramp) or turning the switch off, and a field capacity that code has walked down with falling peaks is raised for a person as a suspected probe fault (PRB-14). — `product-rule` · BRAIN, CTRL, PSO
- **ACT-09** (p2) Probabilities are honest chances over every allowed key and sum to 1; confidence is how well the evidence supports any answer at all; a yes/no answer is the probability that its yes statement is true. A report or a why answer uses only the evidence and the decision record, never presents advice as done, and says what is missing when it cannot answer. — `product-rule` · PSO, BRAIN
- **ACT-10** (p1) Plan adherence (room): code compares the grower's plan with what the room is doing and raises CS-713 itself; asked about the most important drift it found, name what it most likely means (a deliberate change, a plan out of date, a reading holding the plan, a setting outside the plan that disagrees, or no effect today). The answer only picks which of code's suggestions the grower sees; it never moves water, writes a setting or changes the plan. Only when today's plan day is held by a stale reading are you also asked keep_yesterday: whether that reading is a reason to keep yesterday's targets. Code applies today's plan values, the plan's own, only on a firm no, through the envelope, once a photoperiod, never at night, never during a shot, and never by editing the plan. — `product-rule` · CTRL, INTEG, BRAIN

## Brain contract (observer -> planner -> guarded controller -> executor -> audit)

- **BRN-01** (p1) Architecture: an observer estimates plant state from proxy streams and never actuates; a plan or recipe declares targets; a deterministic guarded controller applies freshness, confidence, permission, phase, range and physical-safety gates; an executor runs idempotent commands with read-back; an audit trail records estimate, request, gate result, command and measured result. — `product-rule` · PSO
- **BRN-02** (p1) The model selects within a finite action set that code generates and may explain its choice; it never invents setpoints, edits an approved plan or recipe, or bypasses a gate. An independent validator still decides whether the pick executes. — `product-rule` · PSO
- **BRN-03** (p1) Missing, stale or invalid data blocks the brain's own autonomous actions: fail closed. The controller's water-safety paths are separate: a zone with a dead or set-aside probe still waters, by copying a sibling or on a timer (CT-5). — `product-rule` · PSO, CTRL
- **BRN-04** (p2) Approved plan revisions are immutable. The brain's phase calls, EC steer modes and probe set-asides are directives that expire on their own, and so is a setpoint notch: it is written to the zone's own number as an overlay that goes back to the operator's own value at the lights-on that ends the grow-day it is for. The rescue-shot revert (BR-6), a person's edit, Keep or Undo, or an Auto Setpoints move ends it sooner. Judge from the value the zone holds now, as the evidence shows it. — `product-rule` · PSO, BRAIN
- **BRN-05** (p2) VWC, EC, VPD, light and runoff are proxies for plant state, not measurements of it; every estimate should carry confidence, freshness and what is missing. — `product-rule` · PSO
- **BRN-06** (p3) A notification or chat reply is not an approval. — `product-rule` · PSO
- **BRN-07** (p3) In journal text, call each phase by the words the zone's status tile already shows the grower (listed under the engine helpers: zone_status_label), so the journal and the dashboard agree. Internal keys stay P0-P3. — `product-rule` · PSO, ENGINE
- **BRN-08** (p1) A grow plan is the grower's declared intent. The controller's job is to run it as written and to say plainly when it is not running; drift is reported to the grower, not quietly corrected. — `product-rule` · CTRL, INTEG, BRAIN
- **BRN-09** (p1) A plan day applies at lights-on. A day applied late is better than a day skipped; a day is never applied early, and a plan is never armed, disarmed or edited by the brain. — `product-rule` · CTRL, INTEG, BRAIN
- **BRN-10** (p2) While a plan runs, a setting it controls that is changed by hand has no effect. Treat the change as a sign the grower wants something different: recommend changing the plan's days from today, or disarming; never assume it was a mistake. — `product-rule` · CTRL, INTEG, BRAIN
- **BRN-11** (p2) A missing reading that stops a plan moving on matters only if the engine needs it to water the zone safely. A zone without a moisture reading is watered on a sibling's shots or a timer, and its plan day waits for the reading; root-zone EC is never waited for (the engine waters by moisture without it, with EC sizing and salt checks paused). — `product-rule` · CTRL, INTEG, BRAIN
